papers.title: Relationship Satisfaction Predicts Life Satisfaction Independent of Questionnaire Order: A Preregistered Test of the Focusing Illusion.
papers.abstract: The focusing illusion suggests that making a life domain salient can inflate its weight in global life satisfaction judgments. However, order effects may be weaker for important domains whose information is already chronically accessible. We conducted a preregistered between-subjects experiment (N = 478) to test whether questionnaire order moderates the association between relationship satisfaction and life satisfaction. Participants completed the Satisfaction With Life Scale and the Couple Satisfaction Index in counterbalanced order. Relationship satisfaction was a strong positive predictor of life satisfaction; however, this association did not vary by questionnaire order, and no gender moderation emerged. Bayesian model comparison favored a model including relationship satisfaction without interaction terms. These findings suggest that the association between romantic relationship satisfaction and life satisfaction did not depend on questionnaire order in the present study.

papers.title: Good Things Come to Those Who Wait? Untangling the Role of Memorable Messages for Evangelical Couples Coping with Painful Intercourse During Early Marriage.
papers.abstract: Women who internalize evangelical purity messages face heightened risk for persistent pain or difficulty with penetrative sexual intercourse. Guided by the theory of memorable messages, this qualitative study explores the messages that married evangelical Christian couples believe help and hinder their ability to cope when intercourse is painful or impossible. In-depth individual interviews were conducted with 20 heterosexual couples (40 participants) in which women currently or recently experienced persistent pain during (attempted) intercourse. Interview data were abductively analyzed at the individual level and couple level using flexible coding and assisted by thematic analysis. Nine memorable message types were identified and organized under three suprathemes that reflected how memorable messages functioned in the process of discovering and managing chronic sexual pain: (1) Anticipatory Socialization: From Worst Sin to Best Gift, (2) Communicative Disenfranchisement: When Helping Hurts, and Anticipatory Resilience & Message Disruption: Flipping the Script When the "Switch" Won't Flip. The interpretive findings reveal how memorable messages make their way through romantic relationships to impact individual and dyadic outcomes and illuminate how religious meaning-making may both facilitate and complicate the process of coping with painful sex for evangelical couples. Practically, the findings offer couples, practitioners, and faith leaders possible points of communicative intervention that may empower couples and facilitate adaptive coping.

papers.title: Evolutionary patterns and functional consequences of acetylcholinesterase mutations associated with organophosphate resistance in Panonychus citri.
papers.abstract: Organophosphate insecticides (OPs) inhibit acetylcholinesterase (AChE), and target-site mutations in the Ace gene represent an important resistance mechanism in arthropod pests. However, the evolutionary origins of such mutations and their functional consequences in field populations remain incompletely resolved. Here, we surveyed three nonsynonymous Ace substitutions, A352S, G480A, and Y483W (corresponding to A201S, G328A, and F331W in Torpedo californica), across 31 P. citri field populations sampled from major citrus-growing regions of China. Fragment-specific haplotype analyses revealed close relationships between resistance-associated and susceptible haplotypes, although the unphased fragments limited the determination of full-length haplotype ancestry. Bioassays and binding analyses showed that these substitutions reduced OP binding and produced modest decreases in susceptibility to chlorpyrifos, profenofos, and phoxim, with the Y483W substitution showing the largest effect. Molecular modelling suggested that Y483W may impair insecticide binding through steric hindrance, whereas A352S and G480A may act through indirect structural effects. Moreover, introduction of the corresponding substitutions into Drosophila revealed pronounced fitness-related effects, including reduced fecundity, lower egg-to-adult viability, shortened lifespan, impaired locomotor performance, diminished heat tolerance, and disrupted circadian activity rhythms. Together, these results link field allele distributions and fragment-specific haplotype relationships with the functional effects of AChE substitutions on organophosphate susceptibility, and provide a basis for further investigating how these resistance-associated alleles are maintained in natural populations.

papers.title: Depositional history of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in an arid to semi-arid region of Central Iran: Oil spill and war as time horizon markers.
papers.abstract: This study reconstructs the historical distribution and sources of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) using dated sediment cores from an urban lake and the Zayandehrud River delta in an arid to semi-arid region of central Iran. A total of fifty sediment samples were collected from three cores located at Zobahan Lake (midstream), Shakh-Miyan (mid-delta), and Kooh-Siah (downstream delta). Total PAH concentrations (TPAH26) ranged from 95.4 to 668.5 ng g-1 in Zobahan Lake, 79.3 to 167.9 ng g-1 in Shakh-Miyan, and 98.6 to 241.0 ng g-1 in Kooh-Siah. Diagnostic ratios indicate that PAHs in all cores originate predominantly from mixed petrogenic and pyrogenic sources, while perylene is mainly derived from pyrogenic processes. No consistent long-term increase in PAH concentrations was observed over the past five decades. However, distinct peaks in TPAH26 were identified and linked to major historical events. A recent increase with a dominant petrogenic signature in the upper sediment layers corresponds to an oil spill in April 2008 along the Zayandehrud River. In contrast, an earlier peak with a predominantly pyrogenic signature around 1987 is likely associated with bombing events in Isfahan during the Iran-Iraq war. These findings demonstrate that PAH profiles in low-flux arid environments can preserve clear event-based signals, which can be used as reliable time markers for estimating sedimentation rates. This approach is particularly valuable for overcoming limitations of conventional dating methods in arid and semi-arid regions. Furthermore, temporal variations in PAH flux showed no direct relationship with broader environmental indicators such as population growth and fossil fuel consumption in Isfahan Province.

papers.title: 'So… What Do You Do?': How Gender-(In)Congruence and Occupational Prestige Affect First Impressions.
papers.abstract: People commonly ask potential romantic partners, "what do you do for a living?", yet little is known about how answers to this question affect first impressions. Building on research showing that first impressions can be linked to both the target's adherence to traditional social roles and/or their job's occupational status, the current research is the first to distinguish between the gender congruency and prestige of people's occupations to examine their effect on person perception, including romantic attraction. Participants (N = 245) were randomly assigned to read a vignette describing a potential partner in a male- or female-dominated occupation of high or low prestige and then offer their impressions. Results showed that targets in female-dominated (versus male-dominated) occupations were seen as warmer but less agentic; targets in high- (versus low-) prestige jobs were judged as less warm but more competent and more agentic. In addition, women (versus men) were viewed as less agentic but not significantly different on warmth or competence. Both men and women preferred long-term partners in female-dominated fields. Future directions and implications (e.g., leveraging job characteristics on the dating market) are discussed.

papers.title: Intimate partner violence against women in Ethiopia: An umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Intimate partner violence is a major global public health concern and a serious human rights violation, involving physical, sexual, and psychological abuse within intimate relationships. Worldwide, about one in three women experiences intimate partner violence during their lifetime. Accordingly, this study aims to estimate the overall prevalence and identify the key predictors of intimate partner violence in Ethiopia. METHODS: A comprehensive systematic search was carried out in PubMed, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and African Journals Online to identify relevant systematic reviews and meta-analyses on the prevalence and predictors of intimate partner violence against women in Ethiopia. The methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the AMSTAR-2. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted using STATA version 18 to generate pooled estimates. RESULTS: This umbrella review synthesized evidence from six systematic reviews and meta-analyses comprising 80 primary studies involving 43,785 women. The overall prevalence of intimate partner violence was 35% (95% CI: 28-42%), with substantial heterogeneity across reviews (I2 = 83.48%). It also revealed a prevalence of 32% (95% CI: 26-37%) among pregnant women and 33% (95% CI: 25-40%) during the COVID-19 pandemic. The prevalence of specific forms of violence was estimated at 18% (95% CI: 14-22%) for sexual violence, 19% (95% CI: 15-23%) for physical violence, and 27% (95% CI: 23-31%) for psychological violence. Key predictors of IPV included both partners' and women's educational status, partner alcohol consumption, women's decision-making power, substance use, and income loss during the COVID-19 pandemic, with all associations found to be statistically significant. CONCLUSION: This umbrella review shows that intimate partner violence remains a major public health issue in Ethiopia, affecting over one-third of women. papers.title: Effects of Historical Isolation and Current River Fragmentation on the Genetic Structure of a Freshwater Fish.
papers.abstract: Habitat fragmentation is a major threat to freshwater biodiversity. In river networks, the dendritic structure of drainage systems can compound the effects of barriers to dispersal, which have greatly increased as a result of anthropogenic activities. Yet, disentangling the relative contributions of these natural and anthropogenic barriers remains challenging. We assessed how historical catchment isolation and contemporary river fragmentation jointly shape the genetic structure of a low-dispersal freshwater fish, the Pyrenean minnow (Phoxinus bigerri), across northern Spain by genotyping 280 individuals from five independent catchments at 26 microsatellite loci and analysing genetic structure at regional and within-catchment scales using STRUCTURE. The effects of fragmentation metrics on pairwise genetic differentiation were quantified with Maximum Likelihood Population Effects mixed models, and demographic histories were reconstructed using BOTTLENECK and DIYABC-RF. Strong genetic differentiation among catchments was consistent with long-term isolation, while pronounced substructure within several catchments suggested restricted contemporary connectivity. Among fragmentation metrics, the number of barriers between river reaches emerged as the strongest predictor of genetic differentiation, whereas cumulative barrier height and river distance showed weaker effects. Demographic analyses revealed signatures of recent bottlenecks, likely dating to the post-medieval period and coinciding with intensified human modification of river networks. Together, these findings suggest that contemporary river fragmentation may reinforce genetic differentiation superimposed on older patterns of catchment isolation, highlight the pervasive impact of barriers on connectivity and provide insights relevant for the conservation and management of fragmented freshwater ecosystems.

papers.title: Young People's Perceptions of Technology-Facilitated Coercive Control: The Role of Behavioural Frequency, Impact on the Victim and Participant Gender.
papers.abstract: As digital technologies have been increasingly integrated into everyday life, there has been accompanying evidence of their misuse by individuals engaging in coercive control. Although numerous studies have explored the prevalence of technology-facilitated coercive control (TFCC) in young people's relationships, comparatively little attention has been devoted to how these behaviours are perceived and interpreted. Employing a factorial survey design with 1,010 participants in Australia aged 16 to 25, this study investigated how individual and situational factors shape young people's perceptions of four hypothetical dating scenarios involving TFCC: (a) digital sexual coercion, (b) digital humiliation, (c) digital monitoring and (d) digital harassment and threats. Results indicate that behaviours were perceived as more harmful and less acceptable when they occurred frequently and had a negative impact on the victim. Adjusted associations between gender and perceptions emerged, with young men rating digital sexual coercion and humiliation as less harmful than young women and gender diverse participants. Open-ended responses revealed that young men often justified or minimised these behaviours. Qualitative data further highlighted the role of motive and meaning in shaping participants' interpretations of TFCC behaviours. Overall, the findings underscore the importance of contextual and individual factors in shaping perceptions of TFCC. Implications for TFCC measurement and prevention strategies are discussed.

papers.title: Stillbirth Risk with Class II and III Obesity.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: We sought to analyze the rates of stillbirth at recommended gestational age epochs based on body mass index (BMI) at first prenatal visit. STUDY DESIGN: A total of 79,148 births with optimal dating, BMI at first prenatal visit, and absence of maternal complications (chronic hypertension, pregestational diabetes) or fetal complications (aneuploidy, major fetal malformations, fetal growth restriction) were identified from January 2013 to September 2024. Of these, 33,108 (42%) delivered ≥ 34 weeks with a BMI classified as normal, class II, or class III obesity. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) were calculated due to differences in age, race/ethnicity, and parity. RESULTS: Among patients with class II obesity, no difference in stillbirth was observed compared with normal weight individuals at either early term (370/7 -386/7 weeks) or term (≥ 39 weeks), with aHRs of 2.19 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.67-7.17) and 0.86 (95% CI 0.17-4.34), respectively. Neither were differences found in stillbirth risk for patients with class III obesity compared with normal weight individuals in the late preterm (340/7 -366/7 weeks), early term, or term gestational ages with aHRs of 0.78 (95% CI 0.17-3.57), 2.44 (95% CI 0.61-9.84), and 2.81 (95% CI 0.7-11.28), respectively. CONCLUSION: Based on our results, the utility of antepartum surveillance for the prevention of stillbirth in patients with class II or III obesity may be of limited benefit. KEY POINTS: · There is no significant increased risk of stillbirth in class II obesity at term.. · The utility of antepartum surveillance may be of limited benefit.. · No significant increased risk of stillbirth in class III obesity beginning at preterm gestation has been found..

papers.title: Interpersonal head synchrony in youth at clinical high risk for psychosis during emotional conversations with a close relationship partner.
papers.abstract: Interactive partners have a tendency to align their movements in time during conversation. Known as interpersonal synchrony, this key component of social interaction remains understudied in youth at clinical high risk (CHR) for psychosis, especially in naturalistic and emotional rich interactive contexts. This gap is particularly relevant given the broad alterations in interpersonal functioning in this population. The present study investigated interpersonal synchrony between head movements during three 10-minutes videotaped dyadic conversations (i.e., neutral, conflict, and pleasant) between CHR youth and a close relationship partner as well as typically developing youth and a close relationship partner. The sample consisted of 126 participants, including 29 CHR-Partner dyads and 34 Control-Partner dyads. Head movements were extracted using an open-access video-based tracking tool, and interpersonal head synchrony was computed using Windowed-Cross Correlation analysis. Results revealed that CHR-Partner dyads exhibited reduced strength of interpersonal synchrony (t = -2.07, p < .05, d = -0.53) and increased temporal delay (t = 2.78, p < .05, d = 0.71) compared to Control-Partner dyads during pleasant conversations, but not during neutral or conflict conversations. Importantly, no group differences were observed in overall head movement. Additionally, no significant associations were found between interpersonal head synchrony and clinical symptoms or social functioning. These findings demonstrate that interpersonal head synchrony alterations in CHR can emerge in pleasant interactions with familiar partners. Interpersonal head synchrony may thus represent an ecologically valid, context-sensitive feature in psychosis risk, bridging affective, motor, and interpersonal processes, although longitudinal studies are needed to establish its predictive value.

papers.title: From Invisibility to Self-Determination: Navigating Bisexual Identity, Confronting Discrimination and Exploring Emancipatory Practices.
papers.abstract: In Brazil and in Italy, the rise of the far-right, restrictive geopolitical positions, as well as the operationalization of "anti-gender" politics, are strongly present, affecting the experiences of bisexual women. Nonetheless, nationality remains an underexplored dimension in sexuality studies. Informed by an intersectional theoretical framework, this study sought to explore how Italian and Brazilian bisexual women understand the experience of identifying as bisexual, social support, LGBTQIAP+ spaces, violence, society's perception of bisexuality, and its influence on intimate relationships. The study included 12 bisexual women from Brazil and 23 from Italy. Reflexive thematic analysis was used to identify, analyze, and report themes within the data, with an intersectional feminist lens informing the analyses. Three main themes were identified: Navigating Bisexual Identity; Violence, Discrimination, and Invisibility; and Emancipatory Strategies. By analyzing the dimensions of a transnational matrix of domination, this study offers valuable insights into the experiences of bisexual women in different countries and helps foster a broader understanding of how sexuality, gender, and nationality are interconnected. Moreover, it explores how bisexual identity is constituted through a complex web of power, responding to bi-misogynistic violence and constructing conditions for the agency and affirmation of female bisexuality in Brazil and Italy.

papers.title: Factors associated with anxiety, depression, and suicide risk during pregnancy: a cross-sectional study of pregnant women.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pregnancy is a vital developmental stage during which anxiety, depressive symptoms, and suicide risk may emerge or intensify. Although their prevalence is well documented, there remains a need to identify associated clinical and social risk factors, particularly in contemporary and diverse contexts. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the prevalence of anxiety symptoms, depressive symptoms, and suicide risk among pregnant women, and to analyze associated sociodemographic, obstetric, and psychosocial factors. METHODS: We conducted an observational, analytical, cross-sectional study with a sample of 1775 pregnant women. Emotional symptoms were assessed using the GAD scale, the Beck Depression Inventory, and the suicide module of the MINI. Spearman correlation analyses and binary logistic regression (univariate and multivariate) were performed to identify significant associations. RESULTS: A total of 60.7% of participants presented anxiety symptoms, 39% depressive symptoms, and 11.2% suicide risk. Multivariate factors associated with a higher likelihood of emotional distress included personal or family history of mental health problems (anxietyOR 2.30 and depressionOR 4.15), low social support (anxietyOR 2.25 and depressionOR 3.83), unstable romantic relationships (anxietyOR 2.03 and depressionOR 2.54), recent access to psychological care (anxietyOR 4.69 and depressionOR 4.15) and substance use (depressionOR 1.69). Suicide risk was additionally associated with migrant background (OR 3.24) and high-risk pregnancy (OR 1.81). Nulliparity showed a protective effect against depressive symptoms (OR 0.56). CONCLUSION: The findings reveal a substantial emotional burden during pregnancy and underscore the central role of psychosocial determinants. Systematic perinatal mental health screening-including direct assessment of suicide risk-is recommended, along with interventions that integrate a biopsychosocial approach sensitive to the cultural and relational context of pregnant wo

papers.title: Photoelectrochemical CO2 Reduction to CO by a Molecular Catalyst Attached to Pyrene-Terminated Silicon through Noncovalent Interactions.
papers.abstract: A ruthenium-based CO2 reduction catalyst immobilized on a Si photocathode through noncovalent π-π interactions is active for the photochemical conversion of CO2 to CO, with 34% ± 20% Faradaic efficiency with current densities of j = -(0.3 ± 0.1) mA cm-2 at -1.9 V vs Fc+/0 in an acetonitrile/water electrolyte solution under 1 sun illumination. Si photocathodes were functionalized with pyrene (p-Si-Py) using a Grignard methodology. A previously reported CO2 reduction catalyst, [Ru(tpy)(Mebim-py)(NCCH3)][PF6]2 (tpy = 2,2':6',2″-terpyridine, Mebim-py = 1-methylbenzimidazol-2-ylidene-3-(2'-pyridine)) was modified to include a pyrene moiety in the terpyridine backbone, enabling π-π stacking of the catalyst onto the Si surface to achieve a surface coverage of (1.85 ± 0.28) x 10-12 mol cm-2 (ca. 2% to 5% of a monolayer) as quantified via inductively coupled plasma mass spectroscopy (ICP-MS). A 420 mV photovoltage (Vph) was quantified for the p-Si-Py photocathode. Measurements of charge carrier recombination kinetics through time-resolved infrared spectroscopy indicate that surface attachment of pyrene moieties introduces defects at the Si interface, even without the presence of the catalyst. These defects provide competing kinetic pathways for photogenerated carriers, hypothesized to influence the selectivity of the hybrid photoelectrode, an important implication for future designs of hybrid photoelectrodes.

papers.title: Ligand Field Determines g-Tensor Anisotropy and Radicaloid Character of (L)RuV=O and (L)RuV=N Catalytic Intermediates.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: High-valent metal-oxo and metal-imido species mediate complex chemical transformations, yet their electronic structures remain difficult to characterize experimentally and computationally because of their short-lived nature and pronounced multiconfigurational character. The RuV (S = 1/2) complexes investigated here promote O-O bond formation in water oxidation and enable C(sp3)-H bond amination. Using multiconfigurational CASSCF/NEVPT2 calculations combined with wave function analyses, we demonstrate that g-tensor anisotropy, accessible via EPR measurements, is governed by spin-orbit coupling to low-lying doublet excited states whose energies are determined by the ligand field. Wave function analyses reveal that these transitions originate from the RuV=X (X=O, N) bonding and reflect varying degrees of RuIV-X• oxyl character. Our calculations reproduce the experimentally observed low g-tensor anisotropy of established RuV=O and RuV=N (S = 1/2) species. However, two previously reported highly anisotropic EPR signals are difficult to reconcile with a RuV assignment and can be more readily explained by proposed alternative RuIII species, which have low-lying spin-orbit-coupled excited states giving rise to the high g-tensor anisotropy. Overall results establish a quantitative relationship between the ligand field, which determines the excited-state electronic structure and radicaloid character of RuV=O and RuV=N fragments. These, in addition, manifest themselves in visualized natural orbitals and via spin-orbit selection rules, in the g-tensor anisotropy, elucidating the origins of EPR spectral features of high-valent transition-metal intermediates. Overall, our quantitative analysis establishes low g-tensor anisotropy in the EPR spectrum as a diagnostic spectroscopic signature of a high-valent RuV intermediate, should such a species be generated.

papers.title: Protein-based multidimensional stabilization of nanopesticides.
papers.abstract: Nanopesticides offer new avenues to reduce pesticide application, improve efficacy, and enable precise delivery, but their field translation is constrained by stability across storage, dilution, spraying, environmental exposure, and target deposition. They are susceptible to aggregation, Ostwald ripening, coalescence, photodegradation, thermal/hydrolytic degradation, poor foliar retention, wash-off, and premature release. Conventional surfactant-, polymer-, or inorganic particle-based strategies are limited by mono-functional mechanisms and poor adaptability to coupled multifactorial stresses. As natural amphiphilic macromolecules, proteins possess interfacial adsorption, self-assembly, environmental responsiveness, and biocompatibility. Through synergistic hydrogen bonding, electrostatic interactions, hydrophobic forces, and disulfide reorganization, proteins form adaptive networks that provide five stability dimensions: colloidal stability via steric/electrostatic repulsion; interfacial film stability via dense adsorption layers inhibiting coalescence; environmental stability via protective matrices against UV, thermal, and pH stresses; foliar retention stability via amyloid-like in situ films enhancing adhesion and rainfastness; and functional release stability via stimuli-responsive disassembly and enzyme-triggered degradation. This review summarizes the molecular basis, mechanisms, and advances of protein-mediated stabilization, and further discusses the sustainability, biodegradability, biocompatibility, and environmental safety considerations that will govern its translation toward next-generation sustainable nanopesticide formulations.

papers.title: Record-Breaking Elemental Superconductivity in Tetralayer Kagome Borophene.
papers.abstract: Superconductivity above the liquid-nitrogen temperature remains rare in two-dimensional elemental crystals, where strong covalent bonding often yields high phonon frequencies but insufficient electron-phonon coupling. Here, using first-principles calculations and fully anisotropic Migdal-Eliashberg theory, we predict tetralayer kagome borophene (TKB) stabilized by ABAB covalent stacking, as a liquid-nitrogen-temperature elemental superconductor. With a predicted critical temperature of ∼100-113 K, TKB sets a record-high value among previously reported elemental superconductors. Unlike known high-Tc boron-based superconductors dominated by in-plane σ-bonding states and high-frequency in-plane B-B stretching modes, TKB realizes an out-of-plane s-pz-bonding-mediated pairing mechanism, in which interlayer s-pz bonding states at the Fermi level are strongly coupled to low-frequency out-of-plane vibrations of boron atoms. These results reveal a distinct out-of-plane pairing channel in multilayer borophene and establish covalent stacking engineering as a potential route for high-Tc superconductivity in two-dimensional materials.

papers.title: Finite-Depth Interfacial Coupling in Metal/Topological Insulator van der Waals Heterostructures.
papers.abstract: Metal/topological insulator van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures offer a platform for engineering emergent quantum states beyond isolated layers. While proximity effects in covalently bonded systems are well studied, coupling depth across vdW interfaces remains unclear. Using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and first-principles calculations, we investigate the thickness dependence of TiTe2/Bi2Te3 electronic states. Despite nominally weak vdW bonding, the buried interface induces emergent bands and splitting near a band crossing, consistent with hybridization. Interface-induced features persist in the bilayer, while band evolution nearly saturates in thicker films. Even at four layers, the electronic structure does not simply recover to the intrinsic TiTe2 limit, consistent with finite-depth coupling that substantially reshapes the overlayer bands. Charge redistribution and a moiré-modulated interfacial potential contribute to this reconstruction. Finite-depth coupling may be a hallmark of strongly coupled vdW heterostructures and guide topological and quantum electronic device design.

papers.title: Iron-sulfur functionalization reconstructs the interfacial water on biochar to promote persulfate activation and sulfadiazine degradation.
papers.abstract: Efficient persulfate (PS) activation by biochar is often limited by sluggish interfacial electron transfer and inefficient oxidant utilization. Herein, sugarcane bagasse was converted into Fe-S functionalized biochar (Fe-S-BC) through impregnation-assisted pyrolysis. The optimized Fe-S-BC900/PS system achieved nearly complete sulfadiazine (SDZ) removal after 60 min, with a pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.0645 min-1, 5.7-fold higher than that of Fe-BC900/PS. Fe-S functionalization generated mixed iron sulfide/oxide phases, improved charge-transfer characteristics, and altered surface Fe redox states. Radical and non-radical pathways coexisted, with hydroxyl radical (OH) and singlet oxygen (1O2) dominating SDZ degradation. Interfacial characterization further showed that Fe-S functionalization transformed the surface from hydrophobic to superhydrophilic and reorganized the interfacial hydrogen-bonding network, creating a favorable hydration microenvironment for reactant accessibility and interfacial interactions·H2O/D2O isotope experiments indicated that proton transfer involving water was unlikely to be rate determining. Density functional theory calculations further supported enhanced PS adsorption and O-O bond elongation at representative Fe-S sites. These results highlight the coupled contributions of Fe-S-containing active structures and interfacial hydration to efficient PS activation, providing a promising strategy for designing biomass-derived catalysts for water treatment.

papers.title: Recent advances in aqueous zinc-sulfur batteries: fundamentals, engineering strategies, and perspectives.
papers.abstract: Aqueous zinc-sulfur batteries (AZSBs) have emerged as promising candidates for safe and low-cost energy storage owing to the high theoretical capacity of sulfur, abundant Zn resources, and intrinsic safety of aqueous electrolytes. However, their practical development is severely hindered by the intrinsically sluggish S/ZnS conversion, poor electronic conductivity of both sulfur and ZnS, large reaction polarization, water-induced parasitic reactions, and unstable Zn plating/stripping. Despite recent advances, a systematic understanding of how different engineering strategies regulate these coupled processes remains incomplete. In this review, we first outline the fundamental electrochemistry and reaction mechanisms of AZSBs, followed by a comprehensive discussion of the critical challenges associated with AZSBs. We then comprehensively summarize recent advances in sulfur cathode engineering, including conductive carbon hosts, electrocatalysts, and Se/Te doping, which enhance electron/ion transport and weaken Zn-S bonding. To accelerate sulfur redox kinetics, redox-mediator strategies are subsequently discussed, ranging from conventional iodine redox mediators to various non-iodine mediators that provide alternative reaction pathways while mitigating mediator shuttling. Electrolyte engineering by adding organic co-solvents is further highlighted for its ability to reconstruct Zn2+ solvation, regulate water activity, and simultaneously stabilize Zn-metal interfaces. Other strategies, such as Zn-salt regulation, Zn powder, and gel polymer electrolytes, are also included. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives toward practical AZSBs are discussed.

papers.title: A smart supramolecular gatekeeper: target-triggered compartmentalized cascade for instrument-free chiral discrimination.
papers.abstract: A novel co-assembled supramolecular hydrogel was successfully developed. Through rational molecular design, sodium lauroyl glutamate (SLG) was engineered not only to act as an H-bonding partner for co-assembly with glutathione (GSH), thereby reinforcing the gel network, but also to provide the crucial assembly driving force via its hydrophobic tail. A specific gel-to-sol transition (i.e., macroscopic collapse of the supramolecular network) could be triggered by L-His, whereas the hydrogel remained stable against other amino acids, enabling chiral recognition. Based on this mechanism, the gel dissolution was innovatively integrated with the o-phenanthroline/Fe²⁺ chromogenic reaction. A two-compartment sensing platform was constructed where the encapsulated o-phenanthroline was released upon L-His-triggered gel dissolution and could diffuse into another compartment to form an orange-red complex with Fe²⁺. Consequently, a seamless transition from naked-eye qualitative screening to UV-Vis spectroscopic quantitative detection (with a linear range of 10-100 mM and a detection limit of 1.33 µM) was achieved. The good accuracy and reliability of the sensor were verified through the analysis of real samples (human urine, milk). This work provides a novel and efficient analytical platform for L-His detection, and the great potential of supramolecular hydrogels in intelligent sensing systems is demonstrated.

papers.title: Care-Partner Support Needs During Recovery After Fecal Ostomy Surgery in Older Adults: A Qualitative Study.
papers.journal: Journal of the American College of Surgeons
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Older adults recovering after fecal ostomy surgery may require substantial care-partner support, yet the activities requiring assistance and barriers to obtaining support are poorly understood. We sought to identify care-partner contributions to recovery and opportunities to improve care-partner involvement. STUDY DESIGN: We conducted semi-structured interviews 30-90 days after planned fecal ostomy surgery among adults aged ≥65 years at a tertiary academic medical center. Purposive sampling captured experiences across the aging spectrum and benign and malignant indications. Interviews were analyzed using hybrid inductive-deductive coding and a modified Framework method until thematic saturation was reached. RESULTS: Twenty-one participants completed interviews; median age was 73 years (IQR 68-77), 13 (61.9%) were female, 11 (52.4%) underwent surgery for benign disease, and 10 (47.6%) for colorectal malignancy. Preoperative vulnerabilities included cane/walker use in 5 (23.8%), wheelchair use in 4 (19.0%), >5% weight loss in 10 (47.6%), and polypharmacy in 14 (66.7%). Care-partners provided emotional and psychological support, ostomy-specific assistance, shopping and cooking, transportation and mobility assistance, and cleaning and housework. Participants frequently described variable care-partner availability and unanticipated support needs. Physical distance, reluctance to request assistance, and financial costs to care-partners further constrained support. Most participants supported an intervention to identify care-partners and organize anticipated recovery tasks. CONCLUSIONS: Older adults recovering from fecal ostomy surgery require care-partner support across multiple domains, but support may be unavailable or unanticipated. Explicit preoperative identification of anticipated tasks and available care-partners may improve preparation for postdischarge recovery.

papers.title: Understanding the Partner Landscape for Zoonotic Diseases and Public Health Emergency Preparedness Capacity Strengthening Efforts in Ethiopia.
papers.abstract: Multisectoral collaboration is critical for improving global health security; however, little has been known about how it occurs in order to strengthen public health capacities in low-income settings. We used a multiple case study design to explore multisectoral collaboration in Ethiopia for strengthening public health capacities in 2 cases: public health emergency preparedness and zoonotic diseases. Document analysis and in-depth interviews identified partners for each case and examined partner roles and responsibilities. Partners perceived Ethiopian government entities as leading capacity development, and multisectoral collaboration as important to efforts. Platforms convening sectors and partners, such as the National One Health Steering Committee, were important collaboration facilitators. Institutionalizing multisectoral collaboration can improve leadership awareness and commitment to collaboration. A common understanding of roles and responsibilities in collaboration efforts can also improve accountability, sustainability, and trust. Research findings can improve understanding of how multisectoral collaboration occurs in Ethiopia for public health capacity development. Findings can also provide considerations for strengthening and leveraging multisectoral collaboration to improve public health capacities and systems in other low-income settings. Additional research can expand the evidence base for how multisectoral collaboration increases global health security.

papers.title: Facilitators and barriers to the development and implementation of national rehabilitation strategic plans: a qualitative descriptive study exploring the experiences across 19 Low- and Middle-income countries.
papers.abstract: Purpose: To identify facilitators and barriers to the development and implementation of national rehabilitation strategic plans across five World Health Organization (WHO) regions and 19 low- and middle-income countries. Materials and methods: A qualitative descriptive design was used. Ministry of Health personnel, WHO staff, international consultants, and development partners were purposively sampled. Data were analyzed using directed content analysis. Results: Five shared facilitators were identified: clarity of priorities, processes, impact, and contextual understanding; high-level political commitment, strong Ministry of Health leadership capacity and ownership; WHO's sustained policy influence and diversified support; capacity, interest, and engagement of all relevant stakeholders; and enabling environments and institutional support mechanisms. Three shared barriers were identified: misconceptions and a narrow framing of rehabilitation; long-standing rehabilitation sector challenges; and gaps in rehabilitation data and information systems. Conclusions: Effective leadership, flexible processes, multisectoral collaboration, and prompt international assistance were key facilitators. However, persistent misconceptions about rehabilitation, insufficient data, fragmented governance, and frequent leadership changes were impeding progress and momentum. Aligning leadership, governance, and data systems is essential to move rehabilitation from policy intention to sustained, system-wide implementation. papers.title: A day in sports medicine: addressing rural education deserts in michigan.
papers.journal: Journal of the National Medical Association
papers.abstract: Rural high school students often have limited exposure to healthcare careers, especially sports medicine, contributing to lower pursuit of higher education. This research aims to elicit if early awareness and exposure to sports medicine pathways strengthen student knowledge and interest. Participants filled out a pre-survey using a Likert scale regarding their interest and attitudes towards careers in sports medicine. Students then took a tour of athletic facilities, attended two of three offered didactic sessions and listened to a keynote presentation from a sports medicine physician. Afterwards, individuals filled out a post survey with the same questions as the pre-survey. A total of 15 high school students from rural and underserved regions attended "A Youth Day in Sports Medicine." Comparatively to the pre-event survey, post-event surveys showed that 11 of 15 students (73.3%) reported interest in pursuing a sports medicine career, and 12 of 15 (80%) wanted to learn more about specific pathways.Among respondents, 13 of 14 (92.9%) agreed or strongly agreed that they had a positive learning experience. Overall, 11 of 15 (73.3%) showed increased interest after the program and 13 of 14 (92.9%) expressed interest in attending similar events in the future. 100% of participants reported improved understanding of sports medicine. A Youth Day in Sports Medicine increased students' interest, confidence, and understanding of sports medicine careers. Despite a small cohort, most participants showed greater motivation to explore the field and continue engagement. These results highlight the value of hands-on, mentorship-based outreach for students in rural communities, supporting a basis for expanding and developing future programs. From this research, a pathway program enhances early exposure to sports medicine for rural students, increasing interest, confidence, and understanding while supporting efforts to strengthen and diversify the future healthcare workforce. papers.title: Effects of infertility on relationship quality and mental health outcomes in sub-Saharan Africa: A scoping review.
papers.abstract: Infertility is associated with significant psychosocial challenges, and relationship strain yet remains underprioritized in sub-Saharan African policy and research. We conducted a scoping review to examine the effects of infertility on relationship quality and mental health outcomes among people experiencing infertility in sub-Saharan Africa. We utilized the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology for scoping reviews and reported following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews. We searched databases including PubMed/MEDLINE, CINAHL, Web of Science, JSTOR, Scopus, Academic Search Complete, PsycINFO, and the Psychology and Behavioral Science Collection. Eligible articles focused on the effects of infertility on mental health and relationship quality in women, men, and couples experiencing infertility and were published between January 2000 and November 2025. We extracted data and conducted an iterative narrative synthesis. We included 70 articles: 36 quantitative, 5 mixed methods, and 29 qualitative. Four key themes emerged, which fit within the socio-ecological model: 1) infertility and relationship quality, 2) infertility and mental health, stigma and discrimination, 3) adaptive coping mechanisms, and 4) maladaptive coping mechanisms. Infertility was associated with anxiety, depression, and emotional distress. Studies revealed profound experiences of isolation and grief over unfulfilled reproductive goals, compounded by societal pressures. Diminished relationship quality was a common outcome among individuals with infertility, manifesting as intimate partner violence, verbal and emotional abuse, loss of intimacy, infidelity, and separation or divorce. Couples with infertility attempted multiple care pathways, including religious, biomedical, and traditional care. papers.title: Thematic analysis of dyadic coping in couples managing breastfeeding challenges after gestational diabetes mellitus.
papers.abstract: AIM: This study intended to explore the lived experiences and dyadic coping processes of couples in breastfeeding support for women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). DESIGN: A qualitative dyadic descriptive design was applied. METHODS: A total of 21 postpartum couples were recruited from a tertiary maternity hospital in Shanghai. Joint semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis were conducted under the guidance of an integrated dyadic coping framework. RESULTS: Four themes were summarized. Couples held divergent cognitive appraisals and poor stress communication. They suffered from limited professional knowledge, deficient coping skills and insufficient external support. Both sides had unmet demands for professional guidance, emotional comfort and practical help. Positive dyadic coping strengthened breastfeeding confidence and marital harmony, whereas maladaptive coping triggered psychological burden and relationship conflicts. CONCLUSION: GDM couples experience prominent communication dilemmas and practical obstacles with unmet support needs. Dyadic coping plays a critical role in maternal breastfeeding persistence, mental status and couple relationship. Couple-centered intervention incorporating spousal breastfeeding education is urgently required to reduce stress, promote sustained breastfeeding, and optimize long-term health management for high-risk GDM populations. IMPACT: This study provides empirical evidence for understanding the breastfeeding-related experiences and dyadic coping of GDM couples, and offers a theoretical basis for formulating targeted,couple-centered interventions. It helps to reduce the breastfeeding stress of GDM couples, promote sustained breastfeeding, and improve the long-term health outcomes of GDM mothers and their children, as well as optimize the health management model for high-risk maternal and infant populations. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: not applicable.

papers.title: Dyadic coping as a predictor of positive birth experiences for couples: an explanatory sequential mixed methods study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Partner accompaniment is standard in labour, yet couple interaction and dyadic coping during the high-stress intrapartum period remain underexplored. AIM: To examine correlations between maternal and partner birth experiences and dyadic coping, and to identify specific interactions fostering positive maternal experiences. METHODS: An explanatory sequential mixed-methods study was conducted at a comprehensive hospital in Hangzhou, China. Initially, 268 couples post-vaginal birth completed the Childbirth Experience Questionnaire and Dyadic Coping Inventory. Data were analysed via K-means clustering and paired t-tests. Subsequently, 10 couples from "High-High" and "High-Low" clusters participated in joint in-depth interviews, which were analysed using thematic analysis. FINDINGS: Cluster analysis identified four couple profiles: High-High (32.09%), High-Low (17.90%), Low-High (24.63%), and Low-Low (25.37%). Partners reported significantly higher experience scores (88.98±15.77) than mothers (77.46±19.15, p < 0.001). A strong positive correlation existed between experiences, with common dyadic coping predicting positive experiences for both. Qualitative findings revealed that shared security, physiological synchrony, and joint preparation facilitated positive experiences. However, partners in the "High-Low" cluster often engaged in "self-sacrificing coping", suppressing personal distress during medical crises to ensure maternal safety. CONCLUSION: Maternal and partner birth experiences are intrinsically linked. While effective dyadic coping enhances experiences, partners bear an unrecognised psychological burden during medical decision-making. Midwives should promote couple-centred preparation and targeted intrapartum support to mitigate this burden and foster positive family-centred outcomes.

papers.title: Single-library chromosome-scale diploid assemblies of vole genomes resolve a species-specific duplication implicated in pair bonding.
papers.abstract: Comparing prairie voles (Microtus ochrogaster), a species that forms lasting pair bonds and exhibits biparental care, with meadow voles (Microtus pennsylvanicus), a non-monogamous species showing maternal care only, provides a framework to examine the genomic basis of behavioral divergence over short evolutionary time. Here, we develop a simplified assembly approach combining PacBio HiFi and CiFi sequencing in a single library and run, producing high-quality contiguous chromosome-scale diploid prairie and meadow vole genomes (2.3 Gbp). Comparative analysis reveals substantial differences, including near-complete Y chromosome divergence and a prairie-vole-specific duplication of Avpr1a, a vasopressin receptor gene implicated in social bonding and autism in humans. These extensive genomic changes suggest rapid chromosome evolution as a driver of the dramatic Microtus radiation, generating ∼60 vole species in >2 million years. This single-library approach facilitates a simplified and more affordable assembly workflow, producing near-complete genomes of diverse species using one sequencing platform.

papers.title: Toxicity, health-related quality of life and sexuality after molecular profile-based adjuvant treatment in high-intermediate risk endometrial cancer, PORTEC-4a.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: PORTEC-4a was the first to incorporate molecular-integrated profile-guided adjuvant treatment in early-stage high-intermediate-risk endometrial cancer (EC), demonstrating non-inferiority. Here, adverse events (AE), health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and sexual health are reported. METHODS: 564 patients were randomised to molecular-based adjuvant treatment (n = 367) or standard vaginal brachytherapy (VBT, n = 197). In the molecular-profile arm, patients underwent observation, VBT or pelvic radiotherapy according to molecular-integrated profile. HRQoL and sexual functioning were assessed with EORTC QLQ-C30 and EN24 modules and compared with age-matched normative data. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 58.1 months; 523 (92.7%) patients were evaluable. Grade 1-2 AEs were less frequent in the molecular-profile arm at treatment completion compared with the standard arm (28.3% vs. 45.2%, p < 0.01), without differences in grade 3-4 AEs (p = 0.46). Throughout follow-up, treatment-related grade 3-4 AEs were rare (1% vs. 2%). HRQoL remained comparable to normative data over time. Sexual interest/activity was similar between arms, but lower than normative values. 75.5% of patients reported ≥1 reason for sexual inactivity; disease-related sexual inactivity decreased from 24.2% to 9.2% at 3 years. CONCLUSION: Molecular-guided adjuvant treatment for patients with high-intermediate riskEC is associated with low toxicity, preserved HRQoL and slightly reduced sexual activity due to personal factors (no partner, sex not important in their relationship or partner-related medical issues) rather than their own illness.

papers.title: "I Took the Charge": Coercive Control, Legal Vulnerability, and Intimate Partner Violence Service Navigation Among Black Women Under Community Supervision: A Qualitative Study.
papers.abstract: Black women under community supervision who use drugs experience disproportionately high rates of intimate partner violence (IPV), yet little research has examined how intersecting identities related to race, sexual behavior, substance use, and criminal-legal involvement shape their experiences of IPV and access to services. Guided by Minority Stress Theory, this nested qualitative study explored patterns of IPV and service utilization among Black women under community supervision who have sex with women and men and participated in a prior randomized controlled trial in New York City. Fifteen in-depth, semi-structured interviews were conducted between July and September 2022 via Zoom with women who reported lifetime IPV and drug use. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using a grounded, two-cycle coding approach. Participants described severe and overlapping forms of IPV perpetrated primarily by male partners, including physical, sexual, psychological, and financial abuse. Women also identified coercive tactics not routinely captured in standard IPV measures, including spiritual abuse and "taking a charge" for a partner to avoid his incarceration. Violence within relationships with female partners was often described as mutual or bidirectional. Criminal-legal supervision functioned as both a barrier and facilitator to help-seeking: fear of arrest, probation violations, and prior negative police interactions discouraged reporting, whereas supportive probation or parole officers sometimes facilitated access to services. Participants emphasized that traditional IPV services were insufficient without structural support such as housing, employment, and mental health care. Findings suggest that IPV among Black women under community supervision is embedded within intersecting structural vulnerabilities that shape both coercive control and service navigation. papers.title: Violent injury in children and youth following a mother's experience of violent injury: An evidence and gap map.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Maternal experiences of violent injury may have downstream consequences for children's risk of violent injury. However, research examining links between maternal and pediatric violent injury has not been systematically mapped. OBJECTIVE: To identify, characterize, and synthesize evidence and gaps in studies examining the relationship between a mother's intentional physical or sexual injury and her child's subsequent intentional injury. PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: Children younger than 25 years across any study setting. METHODS: We conducted an evidence and gap map using searches of MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane, and Web of Science from inception to October 2024. Eligible studies examined associations between a mother's intentional physical or sexual injury and her child's subsequent intentional injury. We included observational cohort, cross-sectional, case-control, and secondary analyses of randomized trials. Two reviewers independently screened records and texts, with discrepancies resolved by consensus. Extracted data were used to map evidence concentration and gaps. RESULTS: The search identified 10,298 records, with 48 studies included (93 analyses). Most studies were cross-sectional and survey-based, with limited use of cohort designs or administrative data. Evidence focused on maternal intimate partner violence and child physical injury in household contexts. Few studies examined child sexual injury, community violence, or self-inflicted injury, and none evaluated maternal exposure to community violence. CONCLUSION: Research focuses on maternal intimate partner violence and pediatric physical injury, with limited evidence beyond household contexts and other injury types. Addressing these gaps through broader definitions, longitudinal designs, and diverse data sources is essential to inform clinical care, policy, and prevention. REGISTRATION STATEMENT: The protocol for this EGM was registered on Open Science Framework (doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/4E7U2/).

papers.title: Hearing assistance technologies and social health among individuals with care and support needs: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hearing loss can affect communication, social interaction, participation, and the maintenance of social relationships, particularly among individuals who require care or support in everyday life. Hearing assistance technologies (HATs) may facilitate communication, but their relationship with the multiple dimensions of social health remains insufficiently understood. A multidimensional social-health framework encompassing Capacity, Independence, Social Participation, Structure, Function, and Appraisal provides a basis for examining these relationships beyond individual hearing outcomes. This scoping review aimed to map the existing evidence on HATs in relation to social health among individuals with care and support needs. METHODS: This scoping review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and the methodological framework proposed by Arksey and O'Malley and further refined by Levac. PubMed, CINAHL, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, Ovid MEDLINE, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore were searched. Studies were eligible if they included individuals aged ≥ 18 years with care and support needs and examined HATs in relation to findings relevant to social health. Data were charted and synthesised descriptively, and findings were organised according to the six domains of the multidimensional social-health framework, comprising Capacity, Independence, Social Participation, Structure, Function, and Appraisal. RESULTS: The searches identified 1,145 records, of which 21 studies met the inclusion criteria. The included samples were predominantly older. Findings were most frequently mapped to the Appraisal and Social Participation domains, whereas Structure and Function were comparatively underrepresented. papers.title: Psychometric Properties of the Perinatal Assessment of Paternal Affectivity in Peru: A Screening Measure for the Risk of Paternal Perinatal Psychopathology.
papers.abstract: This study examined the psychometric properties of the Perinatal Assessment of Paternal Affectivity (PAPA) in Peru. The sample comprised 406 fathers of infants aged 0-17 months attending growth and development services in Metropolitan Lima; 58.1% were first-time fathers. They completed the PAPA, the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9), the Parental Stress Scale (PSS), and the Relationship Assessment Scale (RAS). Mean symptom levels were low, with a mild-to-moderate floor effect expected in a community sample. Confirmatory factor analysis supported a unidimensional structure with moderate-to-high loadings and good fit after allowing one residual correlation. The scale showed adequate internal consistency (ordinal α = 0.87; α = 0.81; ω = 0.86). Multi-group analyses supported strict measurement invariance across socioeconomic status and parity. Convergent and concurrent validity were supported by positive correlations with depressive symptoms (PHQ-9) and parental stress (PSS), and negative correlations with satisfaction with the baby and relationship satisfaction (RAS). ROC analysis indicated excellent discriminative capacity for depressive symptomatology (AUC = 0.87; optimal cutoff = 6.5; sensitivity = 0.80; specificity = 0.82). Findings support the PAPA as a brief, reliable, and valid screening measure for paternal perinatal psychopathology in community settings, with caution advised regarding cutoff use until replicated in Peruvian clinical samples. KEY FINDINGS: The PAPA demonstrated a clear unidimensional structure with good model fit in a Peruvian community sample. The scale showed strong convergent and concurrent validity through its associations with depressive symptoms, parental stress, and relationship satisfaction.
